class.name: NetwAuthProtocol
class.brief_description: Wire-format codec for the packets Networked exchanges during [SceneMultiplayer]'s authentication phase.
class.description: Every packet is framed with a four-byte magic prefix naming its purpose, so a session can tell a joining player from a server browser before it reads a single provider byte. A packet matching neither magic is [constant KIND_UNKNOWN] and the receiver fails closed on it, because an auth phase that guesses at an unrecognised packet is an auth phase that can be walked past. Only the provider payload below reaches a [NetwAuthFlow]. [codeblock lang=text] auth packet ┠╴ "NHEL" a player opening a session ┃ ┠╴ version(1) the framing this packet was written against ┃ ┠╴ app_tag(8) the game build folded with the wire identity, ┃ ┃ so a mismatched build is rejected before the ┃ ┃ provider payload is read ┃ ┠╴ flags(1) reserved ┃ ┖╴ provider payload, which is all a flow ever sees ┖╴ "NPRB" a browser asking what this server is ┠╴ version(1) ┖╴ status-or-flags(1), then the reply payload [/codeblock] A probe peer receives a response and disconnects without completing authentication, so it never enters [method MultiplayerPeer.get_unique_id]'s peer list. This class reads and writes the framing for both sides. Every verb is static and the class is never instantiated.

method.name: classify
method.description: Which [enum Kind] [param data]'s magic prefix names. A packet shorter than a header, or carrying neither magic, is [constant KIND_UNKNOWN].

method.name: decode_client_hello
method.description: Reads a hello packet, rejecting it when its build tag differs from [param local_app_tag]. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴ok bool false on a rejection ┠╴reason String "framing", "version" or "app", empty when ok ┠╴version int the framing version the packet carried ┠╴app_tag int the 64-bit build tag the packet carried ┠╴flags int reserved ┖╴provider_payload PackedByteArray empty on a rejection [/codeblock] A rejection still reports the [code]version[/code] and [code]app_tag[/code] it read, so the rejecting side can say what the peer claimed rather than only that it said no.

method.name: decode_probe_reply
method.description: Reads a probe reply. A packet with the wrong magic, a short header, or a foreign version returns [code]ok[/code] false and an empty payload. The status it carries is one value of [enum ProbeStatus]. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴ok bool false on a rejection ┠╴version int the framing version the packet carried ┠╴status int what the server said about returning ┖╴payload PackedByteArray the provider's own reply, empty on a rejection [/codeblock]

method.name: decode_probe_request
method.description: Reads a probe request. A packet with the wrong magic, a short header, or a foreign version returns [code]ok[/code] false. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴ok bool false on a rejection ┠╴version int the framing version the packet carried ┖╴flags int reserved [/codeblock]

method.name: encode_client_hello
method.description: Wraps [param provider_payload] in a hello header stamped with [param app_tag], the 64-bit build tag folded from [member MultiplayerTree.app_id] and the wire identity by [method NetwMultiplayer.auth_set_app_tag]. There is no ungated value. An empty [member MultiplayerTree.app_id] still carries the wire the build speaks, so two builds that disagree about the format or the channel table are rejected whether or not the game named itself. [param flags] is reserved.

method.name: encode_probe_reply
method.description: Wraps [param payload] in a probe-reply header stamped with [param status], one of [enum ProbeStatus].

method.name: encode_probe_request
method.description: Builds a probe request. [param flags] is reserved.

method.name: magic_hello
method.description: The four bytes a hello packet opens with, [code]"NHEL"[/code].

method.name: magic_probe
method.description: The four bytes a probe packet opens with, [code]"NPRB"[/code].

method.name: protocol_version
method.description: The framing version this build writes and is the only one it accepts. It is bumped when the framing changes in a way an older peer cannot read, which is what makes a version mismatch a clean rejection rather than a misparse.

constants.constant: The packet carries neither magic, or is shorter than a header. The receiver fails closed on it.
